solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An unexpected event in part of church? Not entirely

indicators.note: something not entirely present is short of its final part, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the chancel is the area round the altar of a church

explanation.surface: A surprising incident happened in one section of a church, or so it half seems.
explanation.walkthrough: CHANCEL loses its last letter to leave CHANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is a happening that comes about by accident rather than design, a synonym for an unexpected event.

clue.text: Galleries have them in copper and gold surrounded by grasses

indicators.note: one thing surrounded by another sits inside it, so the metal goes within the informers

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a grass is slang for an informer, as is a rat
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Art galleries are said to keep them in metal and gold ringed by lawn plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Grasses here are informers, not lawn plants; Cu is copper's chemical symbol and or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Curators are the staff who look after collections, and every gallery employs them, so the phrase describes them cryptically.

clue.text: Hard to understand when bishop's taken in by pamphlet

indicators.note: a thing taken in by another is swallowed up by it, so the bishop sits inside

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: A bishop's pamphlet turns out to be impenetrable reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is inside the word for 'when', and the pamphlet follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract ideas are theoretical rather than concrete, and so often difficult to grasp; a synonym for the definition.

clue.text: Old cavalry officer finding something hackneyed and French

blocks.note: corn is trite or overused sentimental material
et is French for 'and'

explanation.surface: A retired cavalryman discovers something stale and Gallic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' belongs to the wordplay: the French word for it is ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornet was historically the lowest commissioned rank in a British cavalry troop, who carried the colours.

clue.text: Country doctor looking into innovative AI? Cool

indicators.note: something innovative is new and rearranged, so the letters that follow are put in a fresh order
a person looking into something has their head inside it, so the doctor goes within

blocks.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rural GP examines new artificial intelligence and pronounces it cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country doctor' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Country'. AI and COOL are rearranged to COLOIA and MB goes in to give COLO-MB-IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombia is a nation in north-western South America, an example of a country.

clue.text: Exclude from old university

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone is barred from a former college.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, a direct synonym for exclude.

clue.text: Existing near York perhaps in a shed

blocks.note: a product that is out is available or in existence
York is an example of a royal house, as in the Wars of the Roses

explanation.surface: Something is living close to the city of York, inside a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: York is not the city: it is the royal House of York, so 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An outhouse is a small building outside the main house, essentially a shed or outbuilding.

clue.text: On the point of edging away before the French game

indicators.note: edging away here means removing the edges, so the outer letters are lost

blocks.note: about to means on the point of
les is the French plural 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone is about to sidle off ahead of the French match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the point of' is a phrase meaning 'about to'; only the first word of that phrase is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Boules is a French game of throwing metal balls towards a small target ball, also called pétanque.

clue.text: Having insight into renovation of statue

indicators.note: renovation means remaking something, so the following word's letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone understands how to restore a sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having insight into' reads as one phrase, but 'into' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An astute person is shrewd and perceptive, which is to have insight.

clue.text: With reference to type of repair

blocks.note: re means concerning or regarding
a sort is a kind or type

explanation.surface: A business letter asks what kind of mending is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Repair here is the verb meaning to go somewhere, not to mend.
explanation.definitionFit: To resort to a place is to go there, an old sense of repair, as in 'they repaired to the bar'.

clue.text: Doubt girl's faith

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, with the possessive S
trust is belief or faith

explanation.surface: Someone questions a young woman's religious belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrust is suspicion or lack of confidence, so a synonym for doubt as noun or verb.

clue.text: Experienced Ecstasy then worked on screen

indicators.note: on means attached after, so the drug and the working word follow the checking word

blocks.note: to vet is to check or screen someone
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
ran can mean operated or worked, as a machine does

explanation.surface: An actor high on drugs then performed for the cameras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked on screen' suggests acting, but 'screen' is a verb meaning check; E and RAN are joined on after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long experience, so as an adjective it means experienced.

clue.text: Novelist to let off steam about describing strong desire

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the phrase for letting off steam is read backwards
to describe a shape is to draw round it, so these letters enclose the desire

blocks.note: to vent is to release feelings
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A writer blows off steam while describing a powerful craving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it signals the container, but here it turns the word round; 'describing' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian writer, author of Fathers and Sons, so an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Forms back of coconut shy

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: modes are forms or manners
the final letter of coconut

explanation.surface: Someone shapes the rear of a fairground coconut shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coconut shy' is a fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts; here 'shy' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest person is reserved and self-effacing, a synonym for shy.

clue.text: King unwell complaining bitterly

blocks.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
ailing means ill

explanation.surface: A sick monarch moans resentfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest angrily or rant, so railing describes someone griping with bitterness.

clue.text: Crack found in diamond

blocks.note: first meaning: a lump of crack cocaine is called this in slang
second meaning: slang for a gemstone, especially a diamond

explanation.surface: A flaw is discovered within a gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack looks like a flaw in the stone, but it is the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is drug slang for a piece of crack cocaine and also everyday slang for a large diamond in a ring.

clue.text: About to get Slip and Slide back

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a lapse is a slip or minor error

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to tumble and skid backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'ready to', but 'About' alone is the piece and 'to get' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a former state, such as illness or bad habits, which is to slip backwards.

clue.text: To praise God without also turning up is of little use

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is backwards
without can mean outside, so the praise phrase wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: to bless is to glorify God
too means also

explanation.surface: Worshipping without also showing up to church does little good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking, an old sense the solver may not expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootless is an old word meaning unavailing or useless, from boot in its sense of profit or advantage.

clue.text: Support in spite of employing United's defensive formation

indicators.note: a word employing another makes use of it by holding it inside

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
for can mean despite, as in 'for all his faults'
U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: Fans keep supporting Manchester United's back line in spite of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: A back four is the line of four defenders in a football team; 'for' meaning despite is as in 'for all his faults'.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, the back four is the defensive line of two centre-backs and two full-backs, a common team formation.

clue.text: Short written message about cock-up with dessert

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the written message is read backwards

blocks.note: a note is a brief written message
a cock-up is British slang for a botch or mess

explanation.surface: A brief memo apologises for a blunder over the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton mess is a British pudding of strawberries, cream and broken meringue, named after Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton mess is a traditional English pudding, so an example of a dessert.

clue.text: Absolutely against taking credit

blocks.note: to can mean against or touching, as in 'cheek to cheek'
a tally was a record of goods bought on credit

explanation.surface: Someone is completely opposed to borrowing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' looks like part of the definition phrase 'absolutely against', but the definition is the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely or entirely, which is what absolutely means as an intensifier.

clue.text: Throw out of court over for instance…

indicators.note: over can mean covering, so the court abbreviation spreads round the example phrase

blocks.note: CT is a standard abbreviation for court
as introduces an example, like for instance

explanation.surface: A case is dismissed from court for example, the ellipsis leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 25 across but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast out is to expel or reject, a synonym for throwing someone out.

clue.text: Girl reflective over small badger

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the girl's name is shown backwards

blocks.note: Sarah is a girl's name
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A thoughtful young woman is fretting about a little badger.
explanation.walkthrough: Badger is a verb meaning pester, not the animal; in a down clue 'over' puts the reversed girl above S.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to pester persistently, which is what badgering someone means.

clue.text: Peter out collecting horse right for old dissenter

indicators.note: something collecting another takes it in, so the horse goes inside

blocks.note: to peter out is to fade away or die
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
R is short for right

explanation.surface: A man named Peter leaves, gathering a horse that suits a historic rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter looks like a name but is part of the verb 'peter out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Diggers were a radical 17th-century English group who farmed common land in protest, so a digger is an old dissenter.

clue.text: Make first of excursions in old car

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is used
in places the selected letter inside the vehicle

blocks.note: a crate is slang for an old, decrepit vehicle
the opening letter of excursions

explanation.surface: A first day trip is taken in a vintage motor.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside CRATE after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to bring something into being, which is to make it.

clue.text: …riots organised by a noble

indicators.note: organised means arranged in an order, so the preceding word's letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, disturbances are stirred up by a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristo is a short informal word for an aristocrat. The ellipsis links back to 21 across.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristo is a member of the aristocracy, a synonym for a noble.

clue.text: Complete bunk Nero fabricated

indicators.note: fabricated means made up or constructed, so these letters are assembled in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Total nonsense was invented by the Roman emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like an adjective for the nonsense, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbroken is intact and whole, with nothing missing, which is to be complete.

clue.text: Tricked heartless poet

indicators.note: having no heart means the middle is missing, so the centre letter is cut

blocks.note: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: A cruel poet was swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: DONNE loses its middle N.
explanation.definitionFit: To be done is British slang for being cheated or swindled, as in 'I've been done'.

clue.text: DOGE plan designed for US plant

indicators.note: something designed is shaped to a new pattern, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A government cost-cutting plan is drawn up for an American factory.
explanation.walkthrough: DOGE recalls the US Department of Government Efficiency, and plant suggests a factory; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglepod is a North American milkweed vine with angled seed pods, so a plant native to the US.

clue.text: Lots of soldiers caught in very strong wind

indicators.note: things caught in something are trapped inside it

blocks.note: a gale is a very strong wind
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Many troops are trapped in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in abundance, so it carries the sense of lots of, though it follows its noun.

clue.text: Gave prominence to puddings from the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading right to left, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: desserts are puddings

explanation.surface: Someone highlighted sweet dishes from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Pudding is the British word for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress something is to emphasise it, which is to give it prominence.

clue.text: The most important parts of a football club

blocks.note: first meaning: the core or central parts, as in the heart of the matter
second meaning: the short name of an Edinburgh football club

explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is the usual name of Heart of Midlothian, a Scottish football club in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts are the vital central parts of things, and Hearts is also a Scottish football team, so both senses fit.
